data.name: Manirul
data.gender_notes: Manirul is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manirul is derived from two words: Mani, meaning moon, and Rul, meaning ruler or king. In Hindu mythology, Manirul is a name associated with the moon deity, Chandra, who is known to rule the night sky. The name Manirul carries the meaning “Moon-ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manirul usually hope their child will grow to embody moon-ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the celestial and calming energy of the moon.
data.etymology: Manirul belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon-ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manirul total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Manirul is a name that carries a rich cultural significance in Hinduism, as it is associated with the moon god, Chandra. The moon is an essential element in Hindu cosmology and is revered due to its cyclical nature and its impact on the tides and seasons. The name Manirul implies the divine ruler of the lunar realm, adding an aura of majesty and significance to the name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Manirul represents the divine grace and power embodied in the moon god, Chandra. The moon is considered a symbol of enlightenment, wisdom, and illumination. The name carries the blessings of Chandra, bestowing upon its bearer courage, strength, and the power to overcome challenges. It also represents the cycle of birth, death, and rebirth, reminding one of the transient nature of life and the importance of remaining steadfast in spiritual practice.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Manirul translates to 'Jewel in the Heart'. This name signifies the inner radiance and preciousness of an individual, symbolizing their true value and worth, which is deeply cherished and loved.

historical_references.reference: Manirul was a famous Jain monk and philosopher of the 12th century AD. He was a prominent figure in the Digambara sect of Jainism and is known for his works on Jain philosophy and logic.

Manirul is also believed to be the author of the Jain text 'Manirulatha Prabandha', which is a collection of 112 stanzas in the Tamil language. The text is considered an important work in Jain literature and is studied in Jain monasteries and educational institutions.
